case_title: Rajesh Bhatnagar v. State of Uttarakhand
aggravating_circumstances: Demand for dowry, cruel treatment, unnatural death, false defence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 304-B IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, who were the husband, brother-in-law, and mother-in-law of the deceased woman, were found guilty of her death after pouring kerosene on her. The deceased died an unnatural death within seven years of her marriage. There was persistent demand for dowry items like a refrigerator, television, and cooler, which led to her being subjected to cruelty and ill-treatment. The deceased was found dead in her matrimonial home, and the body was handed over to her family. The accused were found to have absconded after the body was handed over. The prosecution presented evidence including witness statements, medical reports, and physical evidence from the scene, which indicated that the deceased was set on fire. The accused were found to have injuries consistent with struggling or fighting, and there was no evidence of cooking materials in the kitchen, which contradicted their claim of an accidental death. The trial court convicted all three accused under Section 304-B IPC, and the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence.
